methodology_change.reason: D6-C proved bar-level conditional returns are not an executable trade curve: D5.1 reported HIGH volatility gross +34.15bp, D6-C measured +2.28bp; D5/D5.1/D5.2 reported BEAR strongest, D6-C measured BEAR worst at -15.33bp net

cost_first.screen_derivation: SURVIVE needs edge/cost >= 2.0 -> gross 22.5bp; a mean-reversion strategy is not assumed to capture more than one third of the displacement; 22.5 * 3 = 67.5bp

threshold_selection.rule: the most extreme ladder value that still meets the sample floor

normalisation.why_not_quantile_buckets: a decile bucket cannot resolve a tail; this research defines tails

E2.name: EXTREME_BASIS_DISLOCATION
E2.reason: median dislocation 23.5bp at z<=-8 (2.08x cost) and 7.1bp for SHORT at z>=+8 (0.63x cost); full normalisation would not clear the cost-first screen, and the most extreme thresholds fail the sample floor

candidates.hypothesis: a 10 sigma 15 minute fall with open interest simultaneously contracting is forced position closing rather than information; price normalises once the forced selling ends
the same mechanism inverted: a 10 sigma rise with OI contracting is shorts being forced out
candidates.short_justification: forced liquidation is direction agnostic and leaves the same observable shadow (OI contraction); the LONG bias in prior studies was observed on bucket-level mean reversion, never on forced-liquidation events

candidates.hypothesis: HIGH volatility is a state and a volatility shock is an event; D6-C falsified the state version, so only the expansion moment counts
three independent structures at an extreme at once raises the chance a single cause (forced liquidation) pushed all three
candidates.not_a_copy_of_d52_c1: D5.2 C1 was bucket and state based (basis decile, OI 1h fall, HIGH volatility state); C4 is anchored on a 6 sigma 15 minute displacement, uses no volatility state condition, and reuses none of its thresholds

exits.symmetry_rationale: a 1:1 bracket scaled to the event's own size is the minimum-assumption choice; an asymmetric ratio would be untested tuning
exits.max_hold_rationale: 240 bars is the primary-grade horizon already frozen by D5.1, D5.2, D6-A and D6-C; inherited, not chosen on results

intrabar.stop_fill: min(stop_price, bar open) for LONG, max for SHORT
intrabar.target_fill: max(target_price, bar open) for LONG, min for SHORT

costs.funding: actual D2 rates on the 8h UTC grid, engine applied

SURVIVE.rule: OOS VIP0_BASE net mean > 0 and 95% CI lower bound > 0
OOS trades >= 100, all 5 years present, judgeable folds >= 6 (fold trades >= 10)
judgeable folds: gross>0 in >= 2/3, net>0 in >= 1/2
no single trade > 20% of total net sum

verdict_rules.WEAK: S1 passes, at least one other fails

liquidation_future.gate: later of 6 months (2027-03-27) and 30 down events
liquidation_future.future_comparison: Event Strategy V1 (proxy) vs V2 (+ liquidation confirmation)

what_was_computed: feature distributions and robust z tail quantiles
event counts with year and fold coverage
event displacement magnitude in bp (the cost-first screen)

prior_expectation.reason: four consecutive failures on the same market and the same data; this change is methodological, not a new information source
prior_expectation.first_condition_expected_to_break: S1 (CI lower bound) or S5 (year robustness)
prior_expectation.structural_novelty: displacement is 12 to 15 times the cost, so this is the first experiment where cost is not the binding constraint; a failure here would mean no signal rather than too much cost, which is new information
